commands.review_summary:
Adds per-container lifecycle coordination so automatic Docker sandbox and browser rollouts drain active work, retries authenticated browser requests across refresh, and hardens process finalization failures.

PR surface: Source +322, Tests +588, Docs +4. Total +914 across 19 files.

Reproducibility: yes. Current main has a deterministic timestamp-based active-work eviction path, and the PR's queued-cancellation defect follows directly from the exact ordering between the exec tool, runExecProcess, and Docker buildExecSpec.

target.title: fix(sandbox): preserve active work during Docker config rollout
target.body:
Closes #103465
Follow-up: #103542
Filesystem operation-scope follow-up: #103611

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users upgrading an existing Docker sandbox could have an active command or browser operation interrupted when the container's config hash was stale. The old rollout guard inferred activity from a five-minute registry timestamp, so long-running work could be force-removed even though it was still running.

## Why This Change Was Made

Docker sandbox activity now uses one process-local per-container read/write lifecycle coordinator. Exec processes, filesystem bridge commands, and authenticated sandbox browser requests hold shared leases; automatic config rollout claims an exclusive mutation, drains active work, rechecks current container state, and only then replaces it. Explicit `openclaw sandbox recreate` remains an immediate operator action, and an unconfirmed process-wait failure hard-stops the child before releasing its lease.

The sandbox browser bridge now marks only authenticated pre-dispatch refresh responses. The registered loopback client retries those marked requests within the original timeout and abort budget, keeps the same control port while the backing container's mapped CDP port changes, and treats generic or non-loopback `503` responses as terminal. Hung-CDP cleanup queues behind active readers and rechecks the current container and auth token before removal.

## User Impact

Automatic Docker sandbox updates no longer kill active work. Once the real operation finishes, the queued replacement rechecks the container before applying current config. Browser requests that reach the authenticated refresh gate retry transparently across the stable bridge URL, while explicit recreation continues to stop selected runtimes immediately after confirmation.

## Evidence

- Deterministic regressions cover running stale-hash ordinary and browser containers with active leases; neither `rm` nor `create` runs before release.
- Original focused Testbox-through-Crabbox proof on `tbx_01kx5drxa4zj2q82ar4h8r5x6c`: 73 tests passed across process supervision, sandbox coordination/backend/config rollout, exec failure cleanup, and browser bridge auth/activity.
- Follow-up focused proof on `tbx_01kx5n426eevbmdbzkj8st6v1s`: 69 tests passed across sandbox activity/browser lifecycle, browser bridge auth/client retry behavior, and the plugin SDK bridge facade. Exact extension-test typecheck, touched core/extension lint, docs MDX, formatting, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Real Docker drain proof: an Alpine command remained running while graceful removal waited, then exited successfully and the container was removed (`{"during":"running","operationCode":0,"removed":true}`).
- Real Docker browser-rollout proof on `tbx_01kx5n426eevbmdbzkj8st6v1s`: an authenticated marked POST survived replacement of a real labeled browser container; the container ID changed, the bridge rebound to the identical URL, and the POST completed (`{"stableBridgeUrl":true,"containerReplaced":true,"markedPostRetried":true}`).
- `pnpm build`: passed on `tbx_01kx5n426eevbmdbzkj8st6v1s` after the final browser changes. The earlier exact branch build also passed on `tbx_01kx5g8qys4hcm17s9w7dq7w0y` ([Actions run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29078035554)).
- The original exact diff passed `pnpm check:changed`. After the follow-up patch, all four typecheck lanes and the full core lint fan-out passed; final exact touched type/lint/format/docs lanes then passed after two test-only fixture cleanups.
- Fresh structured autoreview on the final local patch reported no findings: `patch is correct` (confidence `0.88`).

## Release Note Context

- Fix Docker sandbox rollout so config-stale containers wait for active exec and browser work before replacement.
- Preserve contributor credit from #103441: thanks @luckylhb90 for the Docker init fix and @aaajiao for the create-arguments rollout design.
- `CHANGELOG.md` is intentionally handled by the central release-prep lane.

Security-owner review is required for the sandbox lifecycle boundary before landing.
